Definition
[Good orbifold and fundamental group] 1. 13.2.3,13.2.5\group foundations Source: thurston:page-0322, thurston:page-0325

An orbifold is good if it has a manifold covering orbifold, and bad otherwise. Its fundamental group is the group of deck transformations of its universal covering orbifold. In particular, if $M$ is simply connected and $O=M/\Gamma $, then $\pi _1(O)=\Gamma $.
Proof

\sketch The definitions identify coverings with subgroups of the deck group. The universal cover, when constructed below, has deck group acting transitively on fibers, giving the asserted fundamental group.

□
